slides.headline: 6 AI PROMPTS THAT FIND THE FEARS, DOUBTS, AND QUIT REASONS HIDING IN YOUR OWN CUSTOMER DATA
1) FIND EVERY FEAR ON YOUR PRODUCT PAGE
slides.body: AI reads your product page like a nervous buyer and finds fears you've never seen. "Here is my product page. List 5 reasons a first-time visitor would hesitate before buying"

slides.headline: 2) DECODE WHAT YOUR REVIEWS ACTUALLY MEAN
slides.body: Customers mean something else when they say 'fine.' This prompt finds it. "Here are my customer reviews [paste all]. Group every complaint and tell me what each reviewer really meant"

slides.headline: 3) PREDICT THEIR NEXT SUPPORT QUESTION
slides.body: Your customers' questions reveal what they're really thinking. "Here are my 20 most recent customer questions [paste]. What is my website failing to explain clearly?"

slides.headline: 4) WRITE THE EMAIL THAT WINS THEM BACK
slides.body: Understand exactly why they left, and this prompt writes the comeback. "A customer canceled because [reason]. Write a short email that fixes their exact concern and offers one fix"

slides.headline: 5) FIND THE QUESTIONS THEY NEVER ASK
slides.body: Your customers' private searches reveal their real doubts about you. "I sell [product] to [audience]. List 10 things they search privately before buying"

slides.headline: 6) MAP YOUR BUYER'S WORST DAY
slides.body: When you know their pain in detail, your marketing writes itself. "I sell [product]. Describe my ideal customer's worst workday. What moment made them finally search for a solution?"

slides.headline: SAVE THIS FOR YOUR NEXT CUSTOMER QUESTION
slides.body: You'll need these prompts the next time a customer cancels, complains, or ghosts you. Daily AI news + real skills you can use tonight

caption:
Swipe for 6 AI prompts that tell you exactly what your customers think, fear, and almost bought 🔮

Find every fear hiding on your product page, decode what your reviews actually mean, predict their next support question, write the email that wins them back, find the questions they never ask out loud, and map your buyer's worst day so your marketing writes itself.

Most businesses guess what their customers want. The ones growing fastest paste their real data into AI and let it tell them. The answers were always there.
